title: Restore shared concurrency for Work Map generated artifacts

phases.objective: Restore the policy-declared shared concurrency key for every Spec Kit Work Map writer while preserving generic governed branch input, exact-head verification, and protected-branch rejection.

e2e_journeys.actor: Repository automation overlap and lifecycle governors
e2e_journeys.entrypoint: The Spec Kit Work Map Autofix workflow is evaluated as a permanent writer of docs/work-maps generated artifacts.
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: The workflow uses the exact shared resource concurrency expression, does not cancel an active writer, accepts a generic governed Git branch input without embedded work-branch literals, and retains bounded publication guards.
steps: Read the Work Map Autofix workflow from the exact candidate tree.
Require the policy-declared shared concurrency expression for dispatch and authorized pull-request contexts.
Validate TARGET_BRANCH with git check-ref-format instead of an embedded branch-prefix allowlist.
Reject main and Production explicitly and require the remote branch head to equal expected_head_sha.
Execute Automation Overlap Guard, Repository Tool Lifecycle Governance, and the focused regression.
assertions: The dispatch-only concurrency key is absent.
The exact policy-declared shared resource concurrency key is present.
In-progress mutation runs are not cancelled.
The permanent workflow contains no embedded gpt, fix, feat, chore, docs, or release work-branch literal.
main and Production remain invalid mutation targets.
Remote branch head must equal expected_head_sha before publication.
No provider call, deployment, database mutation, migration Apply, Production mutation, external send, or force push is introduced.

phases.objective: Verify the overlap analyzer reports no critical resource-group concurrency mismatch and lifecycle reports no branch-specific workflow literal.
Reject future divergence from the canonical concurrency key or reintroduction of embedded work-branch names.
Prove exact-head Draft and Ready workflow cycles.
Confirm main retains the canonical concurrency expression and generic governed branch input after merge.
